## Answer Leak Self-Check

The problem text contains only the statement "Determine whether every non-commutative C*-algebra contains a non-normal element." No solution, hint, sketch, or formalization notes are present. No leak detected. Proceeding.

## Proof

**Claim.** Yes. Every non-commutative C\*-algebra contains a non-normal element.

We prove the contrapositive: if every element of a (complex) C\*-algebra $A$ is normal, then $A$ is commutative.

Assume every $x \in A$ satisfies $x^*x = xx^*$. Fix arbitrary $a, b \in A$. For every scalar $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, the element $a + \lambda b$ is normal, so

$$(a + \lambda b)^*(a + \lambda b) = (a + \lambda b)(a + \lambda b)^*.$$

Expanding both sides:

$$(a^* + \bar{\lambda} b^*)(a + \lambda b) = (a + \lambda b)(a^* + \bar{\lambda} b^*),$$

$$a^*a + \lambda\, a^*b + \bar{\lambda}\, b^*a + |\lambda|^2 b^*b = aa^* + \bar{\lambda}\, ab^* + \lambda\, ba^* + |\lambda|^2 bb^*.$$

Since $a$ and $b$ are themselves normal, $a^*a = aa^*$ and $b^*b = bb^*$, and these cancel, giving

$$\lambda\, a^*b + \bar{\lambda}\, b^*a = \bar{\lambda}\, ab^* + \lambda\, ba^* \qquad \text{for all } \lambda \in \mathbb{C}. \tag{$\ast$}$$

Setting $\lambda = 1$:

$$a^*b + b^*a = ab^* + ba^*. \tag{I}$$

Setting $\lambda = i$ (so $\bar\lambda = -i$):

$$i\, a^*b - i\, b^*a = -i\, ab^* + i\, ba^*,$$

and dividing by $i$:

$$a^*b - b^*a = -ab^* + ba^*. \tag{II}$$

Adding (I) and (II):

$$2\,a^*b = 2\,ba^* \;\Longrightarrow\; a^*b = ba^* \qquad \text{for all } a, b \in A. \tag{$\dagger$}$$

Now apply $(\dagger)$ with $a$ replaced by $a^*$ (which is also an element of $A$):

$$(a^*)^*\, b = b\, (a^*)^* \;\Longrightarrow\; ab = ba \qquad \text{for all } a, b \in A.$$

Hence $A$ is commutative.

By contraposition, if $A$ is **non-commutative**, then it is **not** the case that every element is normal; that is, $A$ contains at least one non-normal element. $\blacksquare$
